title: tenant-onboarding-prefill-advisor-and-safe-defaults
author: Samantha Chen
description:
Motivation: new customers frequently hit suboptimal unit economics when they first start using Redwood due to conservative defaults for batching, caching and quantization. This PR introduces a tenant-focused 'Prefill Advisor' that provides safe, telemetry-backed onboarding defaults and a lightweight dry-run evaluator so we can suggest tenant-specific batch/cache/qprofile presets from day one without risking latency SLOs.

What this PR does (single-line description): implements advisor service, CLI dry-run mode, console suggestions UI hook, and runtime safeguards for suggested defaults.

Key pieces: 1) advisor service that ingests short tenant workload profiles and returns ranked presets (batch shape, cache TTL, kv-prefill window, quant profile) with confidence scores and rollback safety metadata; 2) a dry-run simulator that runs in the control plane to estimate unit-econ delta and P95 latency impact for a given preset; 3) Console integration endpoints to surface suggestions under "Onboarding -> Cost suggestions"; 4) a safe-apply flow that only enables presets in shaded canary for 5% of traffic and auto-rolls back on latency regressions; 5) telemetry hooks and new telemetry views for us to evaluate real-world impact.

Checklist: 
- [x] Advisor core algorithm and schema (proto + validation)
- [x] Dry-run simulator with synthetic warmup and KV-cache model
- [x] Console endpoint and minimal UI payload (front-end wired as placeholder)
- [x] CLI "redwood prefill --dry-run" command and --apply-safe flag
- [x] Unit, integration and e2e smoke tests for core flows
- [x] Telemetry metrics and dashboards (telemetry IDs included)
- [x] Migration doc and runbook for SRE to manage safe apply

Safety notes: the advisor never auto-applies a preset to >5% traffic by default. All applied presets include a revert TTL and automatic latency/regression guardrails (P95 increase > 15ms triggers revert). See docs/runbooks/prefill-advisor.md for operational details.

Performance/telemetry: early synthetic runs show median token-cost reduction 8-14% for onboarding workloads with no measurable P99 regressions in our mini-benchmark harness. Workload sampling and anonymization are applied; no customer prompt text is stored.

Related tickets: ENG-1842 (prefill advisor design), SUP-4123 (customer reported onboarding cost spike).

Migration / rollout plan: feature gating via feature flag "prefill.advisor". We will start with internal tenants + 3 pilot customers, ramp to general availability over 4 weeks with daily telemetry review and rollback windows.

review_thread: Arjun Kapoor: Nice direction — I like the conservative default flow. Two main asks: 1) prove the dry-run estimator under a few bursty workloads (simulate 1k rps/tenant) and 2) ensure the kv-cache TTL proposals don't step on existing tenant cache policies.
Samantha Chen (author): Added a synthetic burst scenario to the simulator and a TTL-compatibility check that marks presets 'incompatible' if tenant policy restricts cache TTL. See commit b3d9f14.
Liam O'Connor: Can we add an integration test that exercises safe-apply -> revert path? We had an incident last quarter where revert didn't fully remove the batch-shape change.
Samantha Chen: Added integration smoke test tests/integration/prefill_dryrun_smoke_test.py and an extra cleanup hook in runtime/guards/prefill_safe_apply.go. Tests included in CI.
Marisol Vega: Security question: advisor collects short workload fingerprints — please confirm no PII or text is persisted. Recommend an extra audit log entry when a preset is applied for a tenant.

Samantha Chen: Confirmed: only histogram/sketch metrics and length/shape metadata stored. Added audit log write on safe-apply and documented retention in runbook. See docs/runbooks/prefill-advisor.md.
Arjun Kapoor: Approving pending CI (one comment: please squash the proto change commits into a single proto migration commit).
CI: unit-tests failed on first run (flaky test tests/scheduler::test_prefill_interaction). Rerun triggered by pipeline — subsequent run passed.
